stem: Which statement best explains why isolated pubic hair does not by itself prove central gonadal activation?

options.text: Pubarche is the response to adrenarche, whereas gonadarche reflects gonadal activation by FSH/LH
Pubic hair only appears after puberty has finished
Pubic hair is the defining sign of ovarian enlargement

explanation: Pubarche is the response to adrenarche. Gonadarche refers to gonadal activation by FSH and LH, so isolated pubic hair does not necessarily indicate central gonadal activation.

rationale: Pubarche and gonadarche are distinct pubertal events. Pubic hair alone does not prove gonadal activation.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because pubarche reflects adrenarche, whereas gonadarche is driven by FSH and LH-mediated gonadal activation.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because pubic hair is a pubertal change, not something that appears only after puberty has ended.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because pubic hair is not a sign of ovarian enlargement.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because pubarche and gonadarche are different processes, not synonyms.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because pubarche occurs in both sexes, not only in boys.
